solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Believe, say, experience needed for this type of surgery

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak a word out loud and keep only the way it rings

parts.note: to buy a story is to believe it
to pass through something is to experience it

explanation.surface: A patient is told that faith and a seasoned hand are needed for a particular operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks BUY (believe, as in 'I don't buy it') as heard rather than spelt, giving BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart surgery that grafts a vessel to route blood round a blockage is named after that detour.

clue.text: Excellent article in French makes money

parts.note: crack means first-rate, as in a crack shot
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A first-rate French grammar point somehow turns into cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash, especially paper banknotes, from the rustling sound they make.

clue.text: Stubborn old beast in a frenzy swallows can

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within another
a frenzied beast is in wild disorder, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An aged, wild animal gulps down a tin can, refusing to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but is the container; 'in a frenzy' scrambles the animal around which 'swallows' places the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who refuses to change their mind: direct synonyms.

clue.text: Support game

definitions.meaning: a structure spanning a gap, or the part of a violin holding up the strings
the card game for four players in partnerships

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a spanning structure that holds things up and a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: After brief caress came face to face with destiny

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a kiss is a caress
to meet someone is to come face to face with them

explanation.surface: A quick embrace leads to a meeting with one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish-derived word for fate, the outcome thought to be fixed in advance.

clue.text: It's said money leads to marked improvement regarding industry for these people

indicators.note: 'It's said' tells us the money word is heard, not seen

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: Reads like an economist's claim that funding sparks a big upturn in industry for some population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes the heads of 'marked improvement regarding industry' for MIRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Himalayan region of Kashmir, a plural people defined loosely by 'these people'.

clue.text: Mark end of circuit with this kind of connection

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on skin

indicators.note: the end of the word circuit is its last letter

explanation.surface: An electrician marks the end of a circuit to show where a certain plug fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A twenty-one-pin European plug formerly used to link televisions with video players.

clue.text: US lawman's line acted regularly as part of handset

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the American West

indicators.note: every other letter of 'line acted' is taken, the even ones

explanation.surface: An American sheriff's lines were delivered at intervals over a telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: The bit of a telephone receiver held against the ear to hear the caller.

clue.text: Measure time — he certainly would in Kansas pen

definitions.text: he certainly would in Kansas pen

parts.note: a yard is an imperial measure of length
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' for time

explanation.surface: Measuring time: the definition says such a person would certainly do so in a Kansas jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition continues the charade: he would certainly do time in a pen (penitentiary). Charlie Parker, the Kansas City saxophonist, was nicknamed Yardbird.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a convict, who serves his time in a penitentiary such as one in Kansas.

clue.text: He danced a series of steps with energy

parts.note: a stair is a flight or series of steps
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dancer moves through a sequence of steps with plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred, the Hollywood star famous for tap and ballroom routines with Ginger Rogers.

clue.text: Type of neckwear sported in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: something sported in a phrase is worn inside it, so the letters sit within those words

explanation.surface: A style of cravat is worn by someone in eastern Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad silk cravat named after the Berkshire racecourse where it was fashionable.

clue.text: Gravity's breaking up meteor heading to Icelandic cape according to mathematical theory

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

indicators.note: a meteor breaking up falls apart, so its letters scatter
the head of the word Icelandic is its first letter

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Gravity tears apart a meteor plunging towards an Icelandic headland, as the theory predicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes, lines and angles.

clue.text: Work unit helps to make detergent

indicators.note: the letters are a part that helps form the following word

explanation.surface: A unit of work is part of what makes a washing powder.
explanation.definitionFit: The CGS physics unit of work or energy, equal to ten-millionth of a joule.

clue.text: Cries hysterically about little chap in muffler

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, another
crying hysterically is wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Len is a short form of Leonard, a chap's name cut down

explanation.surface: Someone sobs wildly about a small boy wrapped in a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muffler' suggests a scarf, but here it is the exhaust or gun device; 'hysterically' jumbles the sobbing word, which goes 'about' the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that deadens the noise of an engine exhaust or a gun, as a muffler does.

clue.text: Concentrate on Italian dictator

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini

explanation.surface: An order to focus on Mussolini.
explanation.definitionFit: In cooking, boiling a sauce down to thicken it is to concentrate or reduce it.

clue.text: Extra exercise with fancy new diet is appropriate

parts.note: ex is a dictionary abbreviation of extra
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: a fancy version is elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: More workouts plus a trendy new eating plan are just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges N and DIET into DIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable or advantageous for the purpose in hand, often with a hint of convenience over principle.

clue.text: Oedipus' daughter destroyed giant one

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A tragic heroine brings down a colossus, a mythic deed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth and Sophocles' tragedy she is the child of the doomed king of Thebes.

clue.text: Asian fish

definitions.meaning: a variant spelling of Thai, a person of Thailand or Siam

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a spelling for a Siamese person and a red sea bream eaten in Japan.

clue.text: Thirst before a meal's small

parts.note: a.p., ante prandium, is the prescription abbreviation for before meals
petite means small, from French

explanation.surface: Reads as the idea that the craving felt ahead of dinner is only slight.
explanation.walkthrough: AP comes from medical Latin on prescriptions: ante prandium.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a strong desire or craving for something, not only drink.

clue.text: As reported catches absolutely nothing

indicators.note: 'As reported' means as heard said, so we keep only the noise of the word

parts.note: nicks means catches or arrests, in police slang

explanation.surface: According to reports, someone catches nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for nothing at all, from German nichts.

clue.text: Top of Nordic piste is redesigned in accordance with others

indicators.note: redesigning a piste lays it out afresh, so the letters change places
the top of a down word is its first letter, here of Nordic

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian ski slope gets a new layout at its upper end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is redesigned' rearranges N (from 'Top of Nordic') plus PISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from marching: moving in step means acting in harmony with everyone else.

clue.text: Sighting of Pluto's centre is blurred

indicators.note: the centre of the five-letter name Pluto is its third letter
a blurred image is distorted, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A telescope's view of the dwarf planet's middle is out of focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is blurred' shuffles OF and U (the middle of Pluto).
explanation.definitionFit: A reported flying saucer is a classic example of a sighting, so the term stands for one.

clue.text: School law can be difficult

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: School regulations can be hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive (comp) is a British state secondary school taking all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate or complicated, and therefore hard to understand or deal with.

clue.text: Unfasten baggage to get sponge

parts.note: to free something is to unfasten it
a load is baggage that is carried

explanation.surface: Unclip the luggage to find a sponge inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others' generosity without paying one's way.

clue.text: Second shot at disheartened keeper going astray

indicators.note: something going astray wanders off course, so its letters are scattered
losing heart means losing the central letters of the word keeper

explanation.surface: A footballer's second attempt on goal, with the goalkeeper demoralised and out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes EP from KEEPER, leaving KEER; 'going astray' rearranges AT plus KEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A film take or photograph shot again is a second attempt at the same scene.

clue.text: Nymphs ultimately spend days cavorting round king

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round another piece
ultimately points to the final letter of the word spend
cavorting is leaping about, so the letters jump around

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Woodland spirits end up spending their days dancing around a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges D (from 'ultimately spend') and DAYS into DYADS, which goes 'round' R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these are tree nymphs, spirits of the woods and oaks.

clue.text: Fine rain starts to trickle over evergreen plant

parts.note: mistle is a less common spelling of mizzle, a fine drizzle

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A drizzle drips on an evergreen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evergreen' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies its own E.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic plant with white berries, hung at Christmas for kissing under.

clue.text: Long walk finds male consuming gin. On the contrary!

indicators.note: consuming takes one thing inside another
this reverses the stated roles: the gin swallows the male, not the other way

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching game

explanation.surface: A hiker's long walk ends with a man drinking gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The gin here is a snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, tiring walk, typically over rough country, is a tramp.

clue.text: International master has to play without a hint

parts.note: IM is the chess title International Master

indicators.note: without means losing the letter a from the word play

explanation.surface: A chess master has to make moves without any clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint is to suggest something indirectly, without saying it outright.

clue.text: Essentially heroes have excessive enthusiasm for country

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle two letters of heroes

parts.note: a mania is an excessive enthusiasm or craze

explanation.surface: Heroes at heart are wildly keen on their homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: He's a kind who could become aggressive

definitions.text: He's a kind who could become aggressive

indicators.note: these words could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about a type of person prone to turning violent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: 'could become' rearranges HESAKIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed youth of a subculture often associated with aggression and violence.

clue.text: Genre of book in small type

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
pie is printing jargon for type jumbled together

explanation.surface: A literary category printed in a tiny font.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE (also spelt pi) is printers' type spilt and mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental book or film designed to make the reader cry.
